PullRequest.Title: chat: allow cloud sandbox creation from the editor window
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Today the editor window can only **discover and resume** existing cloud sandbox sessions; creating a new one requires the Agents window. This PR lets users create a cloud sandbox session directly from the editor's chat session picker, with the same draft experience the Agents window offers (repository, model, mode, approvals).

## Design

A sandbox environment does not exist until it is provisioned, so a new session cannot be drafted under an environment's session type. Instead:

1. The editor registers a single **"Cloud"** creation type (`SessionType.CloudSandbox`). New chats are drafted under it.
2. On first send, `newChatSessionItem` provisions the sandbox (Mission Control task → connect), confirms the draft's picks with the host, and returns an item under the **environment's** session type; the chat infrastructure rebinds the untitled draft to it.
3. Because the draft has no backend, everything the chat input normally reads from a live Agent Host connection is supplied for the draft itself — mirroring the Agents window's own draft layer.

While the sandbox type is registered it replaces the extension's cloud agent in the editor picker, so there is always exactly one "Cloud" entry whose backend follows `chat.agentHost.cloudSandbox.enabled` (as in the Agents window).

## What changed

**Shared (`workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost`)**
- `CloudSandboxSessionContribution` — lifts `_provisionSandbox()` / `trackSessionCreationProgress()` out of the Agents-window subclass so both windows share one provision → seed → connect path; populates the connection customization with `resolveInitialSessionConfig` and `modelIdentifierAliases`.
- `cloudSandboxSessionConfig.ts` — moved here from `vs/sessions` so both windows share the draft vocabulary; adds `resolveCloudSandboxSessionConfig` (host confirmation), `createCloudSandboxDraftOptionGroups`, `readCloudSandboxDraftConfig`.
- `CloudSandboxSessionListController` — tracks provisional repositories and draft config per session; resolves the working directory to the chosen repository, or explicitly leaves it to the host (`null`) for an empty sandbox.
- `EditorCloudSandboxSessionContribution` — the creation type, its option groups (repository / mode / approvals), a `CloudSandboxModels` pool fed by the cloud catalog, "Search Repositories…" (delegates to the extension's picker), and `newChatSessionItem` with a cancellable progress notification.

**Chat infrastructure**
- `AgentHostSessionHandler` — new config hooks `resolveInitialSessionConfig` and `modelIdentifierAliases`; `RequestedWorkingDirectory` lets a type say "host chooses" without local fallbacks.
- `chatServiceImpl` — re-keys the carried intended model when a draft materializes under a different session type.
- `constants.ts` — `isVisibleEditorChatSessionType` hides `copilot-cloud-agent` while `cloud-sandbox` is registered.
- `chatViewPane` — when an empty draft's session type is withdrawn (feature turned off), starts a fresh default draft instead of leaving the picker on a dead type.

**Agents window**
- Host group, creation provider, and workspace icon now use "Cloud" / `$(cloud)` to match; `CloudSandboxSessionsProvider` reuses the shared config validation. No behavior change otherwise.

### Repository picker rules (same as the cloud agent's)
- Single tracked repository (origin first, else first GitHub remote) → no picker.
- Multi-root → one entry per root, in workspace order.
- Empty window / no GitHub remote → "Select Repository" placeholder + "Search Repositories…"; leaving the placeholder starts an empty sandbox.

## How to test

1. Sign in with an account that has cloud sandbox access; enable `chat.agentHost.cloudSandbox.enabled` and `chat.remoteAgentHostsEnabled`.
2. Editor window, chat session picker → **Cloud**. Check the pickers: model (from the cloud catalog), Agent Mode, Approvals, and Repository per the rules above.
3. Send a first message: progress shows "Setting up cloud container" / "Connecting to cloud container"; the draft becomes a live sandbox session running the picked model/mode/approvals.
4. Disable the sandbox setting with an empty Cloud draft open: the picker flips to the extension's Cloud entry.
5. Verify the Agents window still creates sandboxes as before.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run eslint -- <changed files>`, `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed
- Browser unit runner (`node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium --run …`):
  - `editorCloudSandboxContribution.test.ts` — 88 passing
  - `cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.test.ts` + `constants.test.ts` — 146 passing
  - `chatService.test.ts` (`rekeyIntendedModel`, `backfillTransferredModel`) — 8 passing
  - `agentHostFilterService.test.ts` — 30 passing
- The Electron unit runner (`scripts/test.sh`) was not usable in my container due to a pre-existing module-fetch flake that reproduces on `main`; the browser runner was used instead. `copilotChatSessionsProvider.test.ts` could not be loaded by either runner here (import updated for the moved module; typecheck covers it).
- Not covered by unit tests: the chat view pane's draft recovery on feature disable, and end-to-end model/config carry against a live sandbox — please exercise steps 2–4 manually.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The default-option initialization, both resolveSessionConfig call sites, and their sequential first-send call flow are directly visible in the repository. Exact network duration is environment-dependent, which affects severity but not the duplicated boundary mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Remote Agent Host resolveSessionConfig request/response round trips
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost adds one serialized remote round trip for every cloud sandbox first send; N sandbox creations issue 2N configuration resolutions instead of N.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased first-send latency on the provisioning critical path
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The normal AgentHostSessionHandler creation path resolves a non-empty initial configuration once, immediately before createSession. The editor had no separate preflight resolution on that path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every Cloud draft is initialized with default mode and approval options, so draftConfig is normally non-empty. This added line awaits connection.resolveSessionConfig and stores the values; the added resolveInitialSessionConfig hook then supplies the same values to AgentHostSessionHandler, whose _createAndSubscribe path awaits connection.resolveSessionConfig again before createSession.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 411 adds the first awaited remote resolution; the PR also adds resolveInitialSessionConfig forwarding, which feeds those same values into the existing AgentHostSessionHandler resolution path.
Findings.Title: Resolve the draft configuration only once
Findings.Impact: Sending the first prompt to a new Cloud sandbox waits for two sequential remote configuration RPCs after the sandbox connects, adding a full host round trip to an already long setup path for every creation.
Findings.Evidence: ChatSessionsService initializes each option group to its selected/default item, and createCloudSandboxDraftOptionGroups always supplies mode and approval defaults. readCloudSandboxDraftConfig therefore returns a non-empty object for ordinary drafts. Line 411 awaits resolveCloudSandboxSessionConfig, which calls connection.resolveSessionConfig. The result is saved in CloudSandboxSessionListController; CloudSandboxSessionContribution exposes it through resolveInitialSessionConfig; AgentHostSessionHandler merges it into initialConfig and _createAndSubscribe independently awaits this._config.connection.resolveSessionConfig before createSession. These awaits are serialized on the first-send critical path and use the same draft mode/approval values.
Findings.Recommendation: Perform the strict “host did not change the draft picks” comparison at AgentHostSessionHandler's existing resolveSessionConfig step (for example via a validation hook), and remove this preflight call so the authoritative resolution with the prepared working directory serves both validation and creation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or switch to a new Cloud draft in the editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Draft content and option groups are created synchronously. The model catalog request starts on first draft use but is not awaited by content creation; model availability depends on it. If workspace repository resolution is still pending, the draft can render, but first send later waits for all roots.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve or open the Git repository for each workspace root
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one openRepository call per unresolved workspace root for the current observable root set
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The editor sandbox discovery contribution already resolved/opened repositories per workspace root to scope discovered sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not required to render the draft, but all resolutions become a prerequisite of first send through waitForState

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the account-scoped cloud model catalog
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced request per account generation, with explicit retry after failure
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The editor creation type did not exist and therefore did not request the cloud catalog from an editor draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off draft-content creation; required for the model picker to become ready

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of workspace roots and Git remotes per root; effective model-catalog cardinality is one account-scoped request regardless of the number of draft/model providers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Workspace-root repository promises may proceed independently. CloudSandboxModelCatalogService globally coalesces concurrent loads and retains the successful catalog until account change; retries are explicit.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing Git repositories are reused; unresolved roots call openRepository once per observable root entry. The model catalog has a shared positive cache/request promise and is invalidated on account change; failed loads require explicit retry rather than automatic fan-out.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: observable construction, catalog coalescing, and load call sites are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Git repository opening and catalog latency vary with workspace and network state, but both are bounded/coalesced and the new catalog work is first-use rather than eager startup work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: repository boundary cardinality is pre-existing and reused, while the introduced model request is lazy, account-scoped, and coalesced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send the first prompt from an editor Cloud draft
Scenarios.CriticalPath: All workspace repository choices settle; then account lookup, Mission Control task creation, environment connection, content-provider registration, draft-config confirmation, real-session load, repository preparation, backend session creation/subscription, and first-turn dispatch proceed. The two configuration resolutions are serialized and directly delay first progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a Mission Control sandbox task
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One createSession API call per materialized Cloud draft
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Editor drafts could not provision sandboxes; Agents-window creation already performed one equivalent call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Connect to the newly provisioned remote Agent Host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced connection attempt for the new environment address
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Editor creation did not exist; the shared path preserves the prior Agents-window connection behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the environment session type and host config are available

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/validate mode and approval configuration against the remote host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two sequential resolveSessionConfig request/response pairs for each normal draft, because defaults make draftConfig non-empty
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The normal Agent Host creation path performed one authoritative resolution; the PR adds a preflight resolution and then forwards the same values into that existing resolution path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both are awaited after connection and before backend createSession/first-turn dispatch

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prepare the remote working directory, potentially cloning the selected GitHub repository, and create/subscribe the backend agent session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One prepare/create sequence per successful new sandbox session; authentication retry can repeat create once only on auth failure
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This is the existing Agent Host session creation boundary, newly reached by the editor sandbox feature.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the first turn can dispatch

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One environment per first-send materialization. Normal drafts carry two default config keys; retries create another environment. Repository preparation scales with the selected repository size on the remote host, not local session-list size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ChatService coalesces concurrent sends per untitled resource. connect coalesces per environment address, but the create, connect, preflight config resolution, handler config resolution, and backend create operations are sequential on this scenario.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Account/catalog state may be warm; repository choices reuse the observable Git resolutions. There is no cache eliminating either of the two resolveSessionConfig calls. Connection attempts are coalesced per address.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: both remote calls and the forwarding chain are directly traced, and default option initialization proves the common path is non-empty.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote round-trip duration and provisioning/clone time vary by region and repository, but the duplicated configuration RPC and its serial placement are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium latency regression: every ordinary first send performs a redundant serialized remote configuration round trip.

Scenarios.Scenario: Discover and resume existing cloud sandbox sessions in the editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Account-wide discovery seeds providers without connecting. Opening a session establishes its environment connection, lists host sessions, and resolves the existing chat.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One account-wide discovery operation per refresh cycle, not per session row
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing editor sandbox discovery already performed this account-wide scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for fresh remote inventory, but cached inventory can render warm/offline history

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Connect to the selected existing environment and list its host sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced connection per opened environment plus one host session-list refresh per connection/explicit refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing sessions already used the same connect-and-refresh path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to resume live conversation state

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of discovered Mission Control tasks/environments and sessions; workspace filtering uses the effective set of lower-cased GitHub repositories.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Discovery is coordinated by the existing contribution; connections are per selected environment and same-address connection attempts are coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Persisted environment inventory and seeded session summaries support offline/warm listing. Full and incremental discovery retain connected/provisioning environments according to existing reconciliation rules.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: discovery remains account-wide and environment providers retain their existing routing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Inventory size is user-dependent, but the diff does not increase boundary cardinality on resume.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the creation-type registration and shared config helper do not add per-item network fan-out to discovery/resume.

Scenarios.Scenario: Disable cloud sandbox support while an empty Cloud draft is open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Availability change checks the current in-memory model and clears the empty untitled draft so the default type can be selected.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active chat view/model per availability event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous event handling only; no queue or remote work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Disposal withdraws the draft model provider and option groups; account catalog ownership remains in the shared service according to its lifecycle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for performance; the operation is constant-size in-memory work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary is added to this path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a sandbox from the Agents window after provisioning logic is shared
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Account lookup, Mission Control create, provider seed, environment connect, configuration handling, and first-turn dispatch remain the same sequence under the lifted shared method.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and connect a cloud sandbox
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create and one coalesced connect per Agents-window creation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical implementation lived in CloudSandboxAgentHostContribution before being lifted to the shared base.

Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Same per-address connection coalescing and cancellation behavior as before the refactor.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Same persisted inventory, provider cache, and connection ownership as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: deleted and added implementations preserve the boundary sequence.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None relevant to PR causality; this is a code move for the Agents-window path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding and no regression-fix record: the move preserves prior performance behavior rather than fixing a demonstrated shipped regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 25 changed files and all diff pages. One medium finding was submitted for two serialized remote configuration resolutions on every normal editor Cloud first send. Repository discovery, model-catalog loading, existing-session resume, feature-disable cleanup, and Agents-window creation were checked for scaling, caching, lifecycle, and expensive-boundary changes; no other high-confidence regression met the reporting threshold.
